extraction.note: Clause (a) of the adopted premise (HS), synthesis.hadamard-scaling-limit-premise, re-derived in the spacetime algebra on the store's gravitational fields. Standard: this is Prop. 5.6 of H. Sahlmann and R. Verch, Rev. Math. Phys. 13 (2001) 1203, arXiv math-ph/0008029 (statements of Prop. 5.6, Lemma 5.7, Def. 5.1 and Def. 5.3 checked against the arXiv text; the text conversion stops at the opening of their Sec. 5.4, so their Thm. 5.8 and the proof of Prop. 5.6 in Appendix A.5 could not be read and are not followed). The published result already covers every Dirac mass m >= 0 (their Def. 5.3), every globally hyperbolic spacetime and dimension four as a special case; none of that is new here, nor is the independence of the limit from Omega(x0) (gauge covariance). What is new: (1) the spacetime-algebra form on the store's fields (hb, Omega): the identity D_x sigma = hb^{-1}(gamma'(1)), the transport rotor R, the GA Taylor data; (2) the store's dilation x0 + l (x - x0) on the flat background in a gauge with hb(x0) = 1, related to the normal-coordinate dilation by a map Phi_l -> id (computed); (3) Dirac rather than Majorana spinors (their CAR case is posed for Majorana spinors in dimensions 3, 4, 9, 10 mod 8), by an argued transcription through gauge invariance, with the field theory's unit outside the Clifford product on massive lines; the role of their Theta (the matrix of the Dirac conjugation composed with charge conjugation, as the Majorana pairing needs) is taken in the gauge-invariant Dirac form by the constant Dirac adjoint, the e0 of the stored kernels, since the background trivialises the spinors; (4) the limit is identified with the stored normalisation i grad D_+ e0 of the flat-plane restriction result; (5) exact Taylor data on a Weyl-curved plane wave and a generic polynomial field. The equivalence "microlocal condition <=> Hadamard form" used in the proof is the stored Fact (a), their Thm. 5.8, which according to the paper's introduction repairs a gap in Radzikowski's argument that also affects the Dirac equivalence proofs of Koehler, Kratzert and Hollands (Thm. 5.8 itself not checked against the text); K. Sanders, Rev. Math. Phys. 22 (2010), arXiv 0911.1304, also addresses gaps in the Dirac equivalence (both recorded in the Fact at its version 2, with Prop. 5.6 imported there as clause (d)). Imported as the Fact synthesis.imported-hadamard-parametrix-of-the-squared-dirac-operator-leads-with-van-vleck-root-times-spin-transport (cited from memory in version 1): the Hadamard parametrix of a normally hyperbolic operator on a bundle with connection, with leading coefficient Delta^(1/2) times the parallel transport (Friedlander 1975; Bar, Ginoux and Pfaffle 2007, Ch. 2), applied to the squared Dirac operator, whose connection is the spin connection (Lichnerowicz); independence of the Hadamard form from the time function in its i0 prescription (Kay and Wald 1991; Sahlmann and Verch 2001, Sec. 5.1). Cited from memory: continuity of pullbacks under diffeomorphisms converging in C-infinity (a change of variables). Gauge invariance is used to transcribe the Hadamard-form Fact, whose source is posed for Majorana spinors, to the store's pair of two-point functions (argued); quasi-freeness to pass from the two-point functions to the state. Transport-absent (standard quantum field theory on a Gauge Theory Gravity field; R is the Levi-Civita spin transport, not the series' transport); Gauge Theory Gravity is convenient: one global spinor trivialisation and a flat dilation. Its use: (HS) reduces to clause (b), the commutation of the scaling limit with the restriction to the generators of a local Rindler horizon, which this result does not give; synthesis.field-strength-cancels-from-the-leading-null-singularity-of-hadamard-dirac-states-on-null-hypersurfaces treats clause (b) (the leading null singularity on a null hypersurface), using the same two imported analytic inputs; the two cite each other (formal (v) and Step 9 here). The premise (HS) has since been restated (version 3): clause (a), the subject of this result, is retired from it, and clause (b) is now a premise about the restricted parametrix on horizon generators; "clause (a)" and "clause (b)" here name the clauses of its version 2.

levels.formal:
Units $\hbar = c = 1$. Let $(\hb, \Omega)$ be a gravitational field on four-dimensional flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}) whose derived metric $g$ is smooth and globally hyperbolic on a region $U$ of its invertible region, $x_{0} \in U$, in a gauge with $\hb(x_{0}) = 1$ ($\Omega(x_{0})$ arbitrary), and let $\psi$ be the free Dirac field of mass $m_{0} \ge 0$ on it (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-dimock-dirac-car-algebra-on-a-gravitational-field}; Proposition \claimref{field-theory.second-quantisation}), with covariant derivative $D_{a}\psi = a\cdot\nabla\psi + \tfrac12\Omega(a)\psi$ and Dirac operator $D = g^{\mu}D_{e_{\mu}}$, $g^{\mu} = \hb^{T}(e^{\mu})$. The field theory's unit is $I_{4}$ (numbers are read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$); on these kernels, whose values are not even, it stands outside the Clifford product as the right unit $R_{I_{4}} : x \mapsto xI_{4}$, which commutes with every left factor, and numbers act on the right in the same way. Let $\omega$ be a gauge-invariant quasi-free state that is Hadamard (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-microlocal-hadamard-condition}(b)), equivalently whose two-point functions have the Hadamard form (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-dirac-hadamard-form-propagates-and-adiabatic-states-are-hadamard}(a)).
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Hadamard form in the spacetime algebra; standard, Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-hadamard-parametrix-of-the-squared-dirac-operator-leads-with-van-vleck-root-times-spin-transport}, written in the spacetime algebra.)} On a geodesically convex neighbourhood $N$ of $x_{0}$, $\omega(\psi(x)\psi^{\dagger}(x')) = (R_{I_{4}}D_{x} + m_{0})H_{+}(x, x')e_{0} + S_{+}(x, x')$ and $\omega(\psi^{\dagger}(x')\psi(x)) = -(R_{I_{4}}D_{x} + m_{0})H_{-}(x, x')e_{0} + S_{-}(x, x')$, with $S_{\pm}$ of class $C^{1}$ and
\[
H_{\pm} = -\frac{1}{8\pi^{2}}\Bigl(\frac{U}{\sigma_{\pm}} + V\log\sigma_{\pm}\Bigr),\qquad U(x, x') = \Delta^{1/2}(x, x')\,R(x, x'),
\]
where $\sigma$ is the Synge function of $g$ ($\sigma = \tfrac12 Q(x - x')$ on the flat field), $\sigma_{\pm}$ its boundary values with the $\mp I_{4}0$ of a time function (an infinitesimal shift of the separation, written in scalar form: the square of a shifted vector is a number, Theorem \claimref{std-algebra.complexification-is-the-odd-extension}(iii)), $\Delta$ the Van Vleck determinant, $R(x, x')$ the spinor transport rotor along the geodesic $\gamma$ from $x'$ ($t = 0$) to $x$ ($t = 1$), $\dot R = -\tfrac12\Omega(\dot\gamma)R$, $R(x', x') = 1$, and $V$ smooth (on the flat field $V(x, x) = -\tfrac12 m_{0}^{2}$). In this form $D_{x}\sigma = \hb^{-1}(\dot\gamma(1))$, the physical tangent of $\gamma$ at $x$ (proved).
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Taylor data in the store's dilation; computed.)} With $x = x_{0} + l y$, $x' = x_{0} + l y'$, $d = y - y'$, $\bar y = \tfrac12(y + y')$: $\sigma = l^{2}\sigma_{l}(y, y')$ with $\sigma_{l}$ jointly smooth down to $l = 0$ and $\sigma_{l} = \tfrac12 Q(d) + l\,d\cdot\bigl[(\bar y\cdot\nabla)\hb^{-1}\bigr](d)\big|_{x_{0}} + O(l^{2})$ (index reading $\tfrac{l}{2}(\partial_{\rho}g_{\mu\nu})(x_{0})\bar y^{\rho}d^{\mu}d^{\nu}$); $\Delta = 1 + \tfrac{l^{2}}{6}\Ric^{\circ}(d, d) + O(l^{3})$ with $\Ric^{\circ}(d, d) = -d\cdot\mathcal{R}(d)$ at $x_{0}$ (the store's Ricci map; at $x_{0}$ physical and background vectors agree); $R = 1 - \tfrac{l}{2}\Omega(d)(x_{0}) + O(l^{2})$, which is $1 - \tfrac{l^{2}}{2}(\bar y\cdot\nabla)\Omega(d)(x_{0}) + O(l^{3})$ when $\Omega(x_{0}) = 0$. The scaled Dirac operator is $lD = g^{\mu}(x_{0} + ly)(\partial_{y^{\mu}} + \tfrac{l}{2}\Omega(e_{\mu})(x_{0} + ly)) \to \nabla_{y}$, with mass term $lm_{0}$.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(The scaling limit; standard, \cite[Prop.~5.6]{SahlmannVerch2001}, posed there for Majorana spinors with a normal-coordinate dilation and Dirac mass $m \ge 0$; imported as Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-dirac-hadamard-form-propagates-and-adiabatic-states-are-hadamard}(d); re-derived here, proved given the leading coefficient and the independence of the Hadamard form from the time function, Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-hadamard-parametrix-of-the-squared-dirac-operator-leads-with-van-vleck-root-times-spin-transport}.)} For every $m_{0} \ge 0$, at every point, whatever the Weyl and Ricci curvature, as $l \to 0^{+}$, in $\mathcal{D}'$ on a neighbourhood of $(0, 0)$,
\[
l^{3}\,\omega\bigl(\psi(x_{0} + ly)\psi^{\dagger}(x_{0} + ly')\bigr) \to \frac{I_{4}}{2\pi^{2}}\,\frac{(y - y')\,e_{0}}{\bigl(Q(y - y') - I_{4}0\,\ip{y - y'}{e_{0}}\bigr)^{2}} = I_{4}\nabla D_{+}(y - y')\,e_{0},
\]
and the other ordering tends to $-I_{4}\nabla D_{-}(y - y')e_{0}$ (even values, on which $I_{4}$ on the left and on the right agree), $D_{-} = \overline{D_{+}}$: the two-point functions of the vacuum of the massless Dirac field on the flat field in the stored normalisation (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-free-field-spin-statistics-and-guido-longo-theorem}; the kernels of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.bulk-hadamard-states-restrict-to-the-generator-condition-on-flat-null-planes}(ii) at $m_{0} = 0$). Rates, in every gauge with $\hb(x_{0}) = 1$: the leading term converges at rate $l$ (the first derivatives of $\hb^{-1}$ at $x_{0}$); the mass term is $O(l)$; the connection and $D_{x}U$ terms are each $O(l)$ when $\Omega(x_{0}) \ne 0$, but their $O(l)$ parts cancel, so their sum is $O(l^{2})$ (each is $O(l^{2})$ when $\Omega(x_{0}) = 0$); the logarithmic term is $O(l^{2})$ (its $\log l$ part $O(l^{3}\log l)$); the $C^{1}$ remainder is $O(l^{3})$. Only $\hb(x_{0}) = 1$ is needed; $\Omega(x_{0}) = 0$ is not. Since $\omega$ is gauge-invariant and quasi-free, all its $n$-point functions converge: the scaling limit of $\omega$ at $x_{0}$ is the flat massless vacuum. This is clause (a) of (HS) in its version 2, now Theorem \claimref{synthesis.hadamard-scaling-limit-premise}, for every gravitational field in its scope; that clause is now retired from the premise, which is restated as a statement about the Hadamard parametrix restricted to horizon generators.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Normal-coordinate dilation; computed.)} If $N(x)$ are the normal coordinates at $x_{0}$, $\Phi_{l}(y) = l^{-1}N(x_{0} + ly) = y + \tfrac{l}{2}\Gamma(x_{0})(y, y) + O(l^{2})$, where, when $\Omega(x_{0}) = 0$, $\Gamma(x_{0})(a, b) = (a\cdot\nabla\hb^{-1})(b)|_{x_{0}}$; $\Phi_{l}$ tends to the identity with all derivatives, and $\sigma(x_{0}, x) = \tfrac12 Q(N(x))$. So the limit (iii) is the normal-coordinate scaling limit of Sahlmann and Verch, and the role of their $\Theta$ (the matrix of the Dirac conjugation composed with charge conjugation) is taken by the constant Dirac adjoint, the $e_{0}$ above.
\item[(v)] \emph{(What it does not give.)} Not clause (b) of (HS): the restriction of the limit to the flat null plane through $x_{0}$ is the null vacuum by Theorem \claimref{synthesis.bulk-hadamard-states-restrict-to-the-generator-condition-on-flat-null-planes}(ii), but that the restriction to the generators of a local Rindler horizon commutes with the scaling is not shown: the restriction is not a pullback (the wave-front set of the kernel meets the conormal of the null surface along the generators), and (b) scales the generator parameter alone with fixed transverse profiles, while (iii) scales all four directions. Clause (b) is treated by Theorem \claimref{synthesis.field-strength-cancels-from-the-leading-null-singularity-of-hadamard-dirac-states-on-null-hypersurfaces}: the field strength cancels from the coefficient of the leading null singularity of the restricted kernel, restricted kernels of Hadamard states differ by smooth kernels, and what remains is a remainder bound on the restricted parametrix, argued; the premise, restated as that bound, gives clause (b) with this result and that one. (Added later: the bound is proved, and (HS) is now Theorem \claimref{synthesis.hadamard-scaling-limit-premise} (version 4), which assembles this result with the generator results; clause (b) holds for every mass at every point.) Not the ground-state clause of (N$_{+}$), not which state, and nothing beyond the free Dirac field.
\end{enumerate}
levels.technical:
The adopted premise (HS) has two clauses: (a) a gauge-invariant quasi-free Hadamard state of the Dirac field looks, under scaling to a point of a gravitational field, like the flat field's massless vacuum; (b) the same holds on the null generators of every local Rindler horizon through the point, so that scaling and restriction to the horizon commute. This result proves (a) on every globally hyperbolic gravitational field, given two standard analytic inputs imported from the literature (the Hadamard parametrix of the squared Dirac operator and the independence of the Hadamard form from the time function). The premise has since been restated, with (a) retired and (b) posed on the Hadamard parametrix restricted to the null generators, and then proved: (HS) is now a theorem, assembling this result with results on the null generators. In the store, before, only the Weyl-flat massless case was a theorem. The statement is standard: it is Prop. 5.6 of Sahlmann and Verch (2001), who treat Majorana spinors of any mass with a normal-coordinate dilation; what is new is its form in the spacetime algebra on the store's fields, with the store's dilation and Dirac spinors.

The two-point function of a Hadamard state is, near the point, the Dirac operator applied to the Hadamard parametrix of the squared Dirac operator, $-(1/8\pi^{2})(U/\sigma + V\log\sigma)$, plus a smooth term, where $\sigma$ is the Synge function and $U$ is the square root of the Van Vleck determinant times the spinor transport rotor along the geodesic. In the store's gauge, with the gauge field equal to one at the point, scale both arguments by $l$ and the field by $l^{3/2}$. Then $\sigma$ is $l^{2}$ times $\tfrac12 Q(y - y')$ plus $O(l^{3})$, $U$ tends to one, and the Dirac operator of the Synge function is the physical tangent of the geodesic, so the leading term tends to the flat massless kernel $(I_{4}/2\pi^{2})(y - y')e_{0}/Q^{2}$. The mass term vanishes like $l$, the connection and rotor-derivative terms together like $l^{2}$ (whatever the connection at the point), the logarithmic term like $l^{2}$ and the smooth remainder like $l^{3}$. Convergence as distributions follows because the scaled Synge function is the flat square composed with a family of maps converging to the identity. Exact Taylor coefficients on a Weyl-curved plane wave and a generic field check each step. Clause (b), the commutation with the restriction to the generators, is not given: the restriction is not a pullback of distributions, and (b) scales only along the generators.
levels.lay: The series assumed that any state of the free electron field of the standard regular kind (gauge-invariant, quasi-free and Hadamard), looked at closely enough at a point where gravity is present, resembles the empty state of flat space. This result proves that assumption for the bulk of space-time, for massive and massless particles and for every gravitational field with a well-posed causal structure (globally hyperbolic), by redoing in the series' algebra a known theorem of Sahlmann and Verch from the mathematical physics literature: close up, the curvature, the mass and the gravitational connection all fade out of the state's correlations at definite rates. It relies on two standard analytic facts quoted from the literature rather than proved in the series. What it does not prove is the companion statement the series also needs: that the same is true when the state is looked at only along the light rays of a small horizon. That part is not proved here; a later result in the series proves it.
levels.one-liner: Given the Hadamard parametrix of the squared Dirac operator (cited), at every point of every globally hyperbolic gravitational field a gauge-invariant quasi-free Hadamard state of the Dirac field of any mass scales, in a gauge with $\hb(x_{0}) = 1$, to the flat massless vacuum on both orderings (Synge function $\tfrac12 l^{2}Q + O(l^{3})$, $U = \Delta^{1/2}R \to 1$, $D_{x}\sigma$ the physical tangent; mass $O(l)$, connection and $D_{x}U$ together $O(l^{2})$, logarithm $O(l^{2})$, remainder $O(l^{3})$), so clause (a) of (HS) holds: standard (Sahlmann and Verch 2001, Prop. 5.6), re-derived in the spacetime algebra for Dirac spinors; clause (b), restriction to horizon generators, is not given.

proofs.main:
\emph{Set-up.} Take $x_{0} = 0$ by a translation of the labels. Write $x = ly$, $x' = ly'$, $d = y - y'$, $ ar y = 	frac12(y + y')$, $0 < l \le l_{1}$, with $y, y'$ in a ball $B$ such that $lB \subset N$ for $l \le l_{1}$, $N$ a geodesically convex neighbourhood of $x_{0}$ for the derived metric $g_{\mu
u} = g_{\mu}\cdot g_{
u}$, $g_{\mu} = \hb^{-1}(e_{\mu})$ (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}(a), (d); Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}). The Dirac field and its CAR algebra are those of Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-dimock-dirac-car-algebra-on-a-gravitational-field}, with the flat-field conventions of Proposition \claimref{field-theory.second-quantisation}. The scaled field is $\psi^{l}(y) = l^{3/2}\psi(ly)$, so its two-point functions are $l^{3}$ times those of $\psi$ at $(ly, ly')$. Matrix and index forms below are readings of the spacetime-algebra statements.

\emph{Step 1 (the Hadamard form; imported and cited from memory, written in the spacetime algebra).} By Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-dirac-hadamard-form-propagates-and-adiabatic-states-are-hadamard}(a) the two-point functions of a Hadamard state (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-microlocal-hadamard-condition}(b)) have the Hadamard form of Sahlmann and Verch (the Fact is their Thm.~5.8, which according to the introduction of \cite{SahlmannVerch2001} repairs a gap in Radzikowski's argument that also affects the Dirac equivalence proofs of Koehler, Kratzert and Hollands; the statement of Thm.~5.8 was not checked against the text; Sanders \cite{Sanders2010} also addresses gaps in the Dirac equivalence, cited from memory): the Dirac operator applied to a distribution of Hadamard form for the squared operator, plus a remainder that, for the truncation of order $n$, is of class $C^{n}$. The squared operator $(R_{I_{4}}D - m_{0})(R_{I_{4}}D + m_{0}) = -(D^{2} + m_{0}^{2})$ ($R_{I_{4}} : x \mapsto xI_{4}$ the field theory's unit acting on the right, commuting with every left factor; numbers are read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$ and act on the right in the same way) is normally hyperbolic, and by the Lichnerowicz formula its connection is the spin connection $D_{a}\psi = a\cdot
abla\psi + 	frac12\Omega(a)\psi$. For such an operator (standard, Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-hadamard-parametrix-of-the-squared-dirac-operator-leads-with-van-vleck-root-times-spin-transport}(a), (b): Friedlander 1975; Bar, Ginoux and Pfaffle 2007, Ch.~2) the Hadamard parametrix on $N$ is $-	frac{1}{8\pi^{2}}(U/\sigma + V\log\sigma + W)$ with $\sigma$ the Synge function, $U = \Delta^{1/2}P$, $P$ the parallel transport of the connection along the geodesic from $x'$ to $x$, $V, W$ smooth (on the flat field $V(x, x) = -	frac12 m_{0}^{2}$, the value for which $(\Box + m_{0}^{2})(1/\sigma + V\log\sigma)$ has no $1/\sigma$ term, since $\Box\log\sigma = \Box\sigma/\sigma - Q(
abla\sigma)/\sigma^{2} = 2/\sigma$; computed); the constant $-	frac{1}{8\pi^{2}}$ is fixed by the flat case (Step 6). Parallel transport of a spinor along $\gamma$ solves $\dot\gamma\cdot
abla\psi + 	frac12\Omega(\dot\gamma)\psi = 0$, so $P$ is left multiplication by the rotor $R$ with $\dot R = -	frac12\Omega(\dot\gamma)R$, $R = 1$ at $t = 0$ ($R	ilde R = 1$ since $\Omega(\dot\gamma)$ is a bivector). The boundary values $\sigma_{\pm}$ carry the $I_{4}0$ of a time function, an infinitesimal shift of the separation written in scalar form; the limit does not depend on which time function (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-hadamard-parametrix-of-the-squared-dirac-operator-leads-with-van-vleck-root-times-spin-transport}(c): Kay and Wald 1991; Sahlmann and Verch, Sec.~5.1). Positive frequency is fixed as in the stored flat kernels (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.bulk-hadamard-states-restrict-to-the-generator-condition-on-flat-null-planes}(ii)): $\omega(\psi\psi^{\dagger})$ carries $(p + m_{0})e_{0}e^{-I_{4}p\cdot z}$, $p = R_{I_{4}}
abla$ on $e^{-I_{4}p\cdot z}$, whence $(R_{I_{4}}D_{x} + m_{0})H_{+}e_{0}$; the other ordering carries $(p - m_{0})e_{0}e^{+I_{4}p\cdot z}$, $p = -R_{I_{4}}
